messages:
jess: Quick question for security/legal 11 We want to enable an opt-in debug capture for /v2/infer responses next week. Analytics needs to inspect a handful of raw response bodies (no logs exported) for up to 24h to triage an output regression. Can Product get a one-time access window to S3 with strict IAM & TTL? Looking for a quick yes/no and any required checklist.

sam_security: Short answer: allowed only with approvals + enforced protections. Requirements: (1) client-side header/token masking before capture, (2) automated PII scrubbing or flagging, (3) S3 bucket with SSE, access via temporary role (aws-sso) and MFA, (4) 24h TTL lifecycle, (5) audit trail of viewers. No manual exports without explicit approval. Ping me when PR ready.

ben_eng: @jess will the capture include original prompts? If prompts may contain emails/SSNs we should never persist them in raw form. For debugging we can capture response delta + context hashes instead of full prompts.

jess: ben 11 The regression reproduces only when customer prompts include identifiers. Analytics insists on seeing the full response to verify our post-processing didn't strip a token. They claimed it's blocking a GA date.

sara_legal: If customer PII is in scope we need: (A) product owner justification (one paragraph), (B) PO signature, (C) confirmation of applicable contracts and regional constraints (e.g., EU/Schengen). If data is internally generated (no customer IDs) it's lower friction but still needs minimal retention and viewer logging.

security-bot: New audit ticket created: INC-20260317-77. Attach the access request and approvals here. Approval required from @sara_legal and @noah_privacy.

marta_analytics: We can accept not seeing prompts. Our only need is the raw response text. Proposed safe workflow: (1) infra flag to sample N responses to encrypted S3; (2) automated scrub run before persistence (regex-based); (3) TTL 24h; (4) access via analytics-debug role only; (5) notify security on access. Is that acceptable?

noah_privacy: That looks reasonable with caveats: add both pattern-based scrubs and entropy detection (to catch weird UUIDs/IDs). If anything matches the sensitive patterns, either redact or escalate to legal. Example patterns we use:\n\nconst SCRUB_PATTERNS = [\n  /[a-z0-9._%+-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+\\.[a-z]{2,}/gi, // email\n  /\\b\\d{3}-\\d{2}-\\d{4}\\b/g, // SSN-like\n  /\\+?\\d[\\d\\s().-]{7,}\\d/g // phone-like\n];\n\nAnything caught must be reviewed and cannot be exported.

ben_eng: Implementation note: infra already has a sampling hook in the infer path. I'll add the regex scrub lambda and lifecycle rule. Will open a PR and tag @sam_security for IAM review. We can also drop prompts from capture at the agent layer.

sara_legal: Conditional approval: legal OK if PO justification + access limited to 24h + no export clause documented. Also need to confirm whether any EU customer data could be in samples. Ill sign once PO posts the justification doc link.

sam_security: I'll review the PR for least-privilege IAM & S3 policies. Must include bucket policies to block public ACLs, enforce SSE, and enable access logging. Require MFA on the analytics role during the access window.

jess: Next steps: ben to open PR for the scrub + TTL, sam to review IAM, marta to file formal access request, sara to sign the legal note. I'll hold the rollout until approval chain is complete. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:

marta_analytics: Filed access request: https://internal-requests/requisitions/8921. Tagging @jess as PO.

ben_eng: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2012 11 adds SCRUB_PATTERNS + lifecycle rule + disables prompt capture. @sam_security PTAL, ETA merge tomorrow.

sam_security: Reviewing now. If scrub runs pre-persistence and prompt capture is disabled, I can sign off quickly. :eyes:

security-bot: NOTE: Access only granted once approvals are recorded on INC-20260317-77. Manual exports will require additional sign-off.

jess: Logging this thread for audit. If anything changes post-approval, update here so the ticket has a single source. Thanks.
